خَصِرٌ , applied to a day, Painfully cold. (A, TA.) ―
-b2- Cold, as an epithet, (S, K,) applied to water, (S,) and to anything. (TA.) ―
-b3- A man feeling cold [especially in his extremities: see 1]: to signify cold and hungry, the epithet خَرِصٌ is used. (A 'Obeyd.) ―
-b4- ثَغْرٌ خَصِرٌ [A mouth, or front teeth,] cold, or cool, in the place that is hissed. (A, TA. [See also مُخَصَّرٌ.])
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
